Ezem@Jos.15.29-1Ch.description: Ezem, a city allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon in the Negev region.
Ezem@Jos.15.29-1Ch.name: Ezem

Ezer@1Ch.12.9.description: Ezer was a Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from King Saul.
Ezer@1Ch.12.9.name: Ezer

Ezer@1Ch.4.4.description: Ezer was the father or founder of Hushah and a son of Hur of Ephrathah.
Ezer@1Ch.4.4.name: Ezer

Ezer@1Ch.7.21.description: Ezer was a son of Ephraim who was killed by the men of Gath while attempting to steal their livestock.
Ezer@1Ch.7.21.name: Ezer

Ezer@Gen.36.21-1Ch.description: Ezer was a Horite chief in the land of Seir, a son of Seir the Horite.
Ezer@Gen.36.21-1Ch.name: Ezer

Ezer@Neh.12.42.description: Ezer was a Levite who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall during the time of Nehemiah.
Ezer@Neh.12.42.name: Ezer

Ezer@Neh.3.19.description: Ezer, the ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section of Jerusalem's wall near the armory.
Ezer@Neh.3.19.name: Ezer

Ezion-geber@Num.33.35-2Ch.description: Ezion-geber, an Israelite encampment during the Exodus and later a port city on the Red Sea, known for its maritime trade and shipbuilding.
Ezion-geber@Num.33.35-2Ch.name: Ezion-geber

Eznites@2Sa.23.8.description: Adino the Eznite, also known as Josheb-Basshebeth, was one of David's mighty men who wielded his spear against eight hundred men.
Eznites@2Sa.23.8.name: Eznites

Ezra@Ezr.7.1-Neh.description: Ezra was a priest and scribe who led a group of Jewish exiles back to Jerusalem and played a key role in the spiritual reformation of the people.
Ezra@Ezr.7.1-Neh.name: Ezra

Ezra@Neh.12.1-.description: Ezra was a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
Ezra@Neh.12.1-.name: Ezra

Ezrah@1Ch.4.17.description: Ezrah was a son of Chelub, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
Ezrah@1Ch.4.17.name: Ezrah

Ezri@1Ch.27.26.description: Ezri was the overseer of King David's agricultural workers who tilled the soil.
Ezri@1Ch.27.26.name: Ezri
